html:
SMTO-GML-0009 — The list of emails to change has expired

GUID: 07f376d6-9b9f-4c2b-bbb0-5a051e46961f
Slug: gmail-bulk-selection-expired
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO had prepared a list of emails to change, but that list is no longer valid. It lasts 10 minutes, works only once, and is cleared when SMTO restarts. Nothing was changed by this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail and look at a few of the emails you meant to change, for example whether they were archived, marked read or labeled. If SMTO already used this list once, the change may have been made.
  2. If the change is not there, ask SMTO to show you the matching emails again and make the change. A fresh list reflects your mailbox as it is now.
  3. Approve the new list within a few minutes after you check it. A list expires 10 minutes after it is made.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports how many emails it changed, and Gmail shows the change on them.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't reconnect or sign in to your Gmail account again to fix this; your account is fine.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • gmail.batch_modify received a selection_token that is not in the Server's in-memory selection registry: it passed its 10-minute expiry, was already consumed by an earlier batch_modify call, or was lost when the Server restarted.

What this means

  • A bulk selection token is absent from the retained selection registry or its monotonic expiry has passed. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • A bulk selection token is absent from the retained selection registry or its monotonic expiry has passed.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the original preview identity and lifetime; a token may also have been consumed by an earlier attempt.

How to fix it

  • Treat the old selection_token as dead. If it was consumed by an earlier batch_modify, verify in Gmail whether that change was applied; then run gmail.preview_modify again with the same account, operation and label and use the new token after user approval. Do not sign in again the account to fix this.
  • Refresh the search and preview, then confirm the new authoritative selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Original effects are reconciled and any intended new selection receives a fresh preview/confirmation.

What not to do

  • Do not reauthenticate the account merely to repair an expired selection.
  • Do not reuse the expired selection token.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GML-0036 — Google refused SMTO access to this Gmail request
  • SMTO-GML-0026 — Gmail authorization expired
  • SMTO-GML-0030 — Gmail mutation outcome is unknown
